answer: A single glacier checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 111 aliases therefore costs 233 bonds held for 13 days each, plus the mirror attestations those aliases can never earn. Each identity must lock a bond, called a ripple, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
